# Removed tmux tab-discovery tests

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

Considered whether removing tab ordering, deduplication and agent-window exclusion tests lets a shell tab point at the agent or another session, potentially ending user work when closed. The replacement path retains the relevant identity and ordering protections.

## Details

Suggested bucket: highest if that destructive route existed. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this deletion concern; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation, not specification acceptance alone. possible_cover: none known; coverage sources not searched.

The assigned deletion is parent terminals.rs:3828–3966 (patch packet lines 1–139). git grep at the reviewed revision finds no tabs_from_pane_states in the supervisor source. Replacement terminals.rs:223–247 resolves tabs only from the session's host-tab cell. core/host_tabs.rs:258–277 sorts tabs by creation stamp and tab id; :337–355 assigns a monotonic stamp. :1279–1471 restores tab entries from launch records, skips held session/tab ids, and requires names_tab before adoption. :1476–1478 requires the exact session id, tab id and HostRole::Tab. :400–446 constructs fresh tabs using a new UUID and HostRole::Tab. :915–928 confirms the selected runtime still belongs to that tab and refuses the agent runtime before close. The current host ordering test remains at host_tabs.rs:1735–1800, with a separate creation-stamp test at :1817–1826.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:2332–2333, Terminal host / Tabs in hosts, says exactly: "Closing a tab: the session's cell holds only hosts whose tag names one of its tabs (the open wrote it, a reload checked it), and the agent's own runtime is refused". The deleted numeric pane/window ordering and split-pane deduplication tests no longer exercise any shipped path: a terminal host owns one terminal.

Caveats: this validates the removal's identity/order consequences, not all host implementation paths or arbitrary hostile state mutation. No independent retired-code defects were investigated. No tests or reproductions executed. This revision supplies original line references and the exact contract quotation; it preserves the originally considered loss-of-work consequence.

# Removed tmux tab-discovery tests

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

Considered whether removing discovery and agent-exclusion tests permits closing a shell tab to end the agent or another session's user work. That potentially highest consequence remains the reason for independent review of this proposed drop; no such route has been established.

## Details

Suggested bucket: highest if the wrong-tab-close route existed. Could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the removal concern, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation, pending the parent's independent check; no parent acceptance is claimed. possible_cover: none known; prohibited coverage sources not searched.

The deleted cases are parent terminals.rs:3828–3966, assigned patch lines 1–139. Their numeric window/pane ordering, split-pane deduplication and mutable tmux-marker exclusion mechanics are retired. Necessary behaviors remain tab creation order and keeping the agent/other sessions outside a tab-close target. terminals.rs:223–247 resolves through the session's host-tab cell. core/host_tabs.rs:258–277 orders by creation stamp/tab id, :337–355 generates a stamp after every known stamp, and :400–446 creates an explicit HostRole::Tab. Existing tests at :1744–1799 assert exact listing order and filtering; :1818–1824 asserts a future existing stamp cannot reorder the next open. These are actual current service-cell oracles, rather than merely equivalent comments.

Synthesis checked all replacement adoption entrances: initial scan at host_tabs.rs:1404–1406, retry scan at :1137–1142, and settling an interrupted start at :1553–1569 each require names_tab (:1476–1478: exact session id, tab id and HostRole::Tab). A nonmatching readable tag becomes an unavailable placeholder, not an adopted runtime (:1423–1434, :1145–1151, :1571–1578). Retry installation at :1176–1206 requires the same session cell, old handle and tab id, and aborts an uninstalled replacement. Close at :915–928 revalidates the tab's runtime and refuses the agent runtime. The tag role is an enum (hosts/tag.rs:60–86), so an agent/tag cannot simultaneously carry the old tmux tests' two independent markers.

Additional test-source check: hosts/registry/tests.rs:531–579 supplies an agent plus four tab hosts, asserts exact stamp order excluding the agent and flags a duplicate tab id. The registry helper at hosts/registry.rs:622–656 implements that test, but production adopt_tab_hosts uses per-record by_name/names_tab, not registry.tabs; therefore this is not claimed as a direct oracle for the production per-record rejection branch. No direct test of every names_tab refusal was established by the targeted search. The removed tmux tests never exercised those host branches, so their removal is not evidence that a previously tested host behavior lost its oracle. This distinction narrows the conclusion rather than certifying the complete host test suite.

Contract remains SPEC_impl.md:2332–2333, Terminal host / Tabs in hosts: "Closing a tab: the session's cell holds only hosts whose tag names one of its tabs (the open wrote it, a reload checked it), and the agent's own runtime is refused". All readily checkable identity/order premises above were checked against pinned source. No tests or reproductions executed. No independent retired-code defects investigated.

# Removed tmux sink lifecycle tests

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

Considered whether deleting indefinite sink retry, child-reaping, cancellation-safe handoff, failure poisoning and healthy-backoff-reset tests permits stuck output, leaked clients or overlap during terminal reconnect. A viewer reconnect now uses the existing host reader rather than replacing an external sink client.

## Details

Suggested bucket: high for materially stuck output if established. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this test removal. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this deletion concern, not observed execution. proposed_drop: source refutation. possible_cover: none known; coverage sources not searched.

Assigned patch lines 141–991 remove sink tests and helpers (parent terminals.rs:3969 through the final sink test before :4820). git grep finds no SessionSink, run_session_sink, SinkRegistry or sink_retry_delay anywhere under the reviewed supervisor src tree. HostTerminal is an Arc handle at hosts/terminal.rs:1226–1280. Adoption creates the runtime at :1772–1938 and spawns runtime.run(conn) at :1926; Runtime::run at :3031–3053 drives the host connection independently of viewer attachments and reconnects on connection errors. handlers.rs:1688–1717 resolves an existing terminal and requires grid support before takeover. :1935–1974 starts only an in-process HostAttach pump and GridSender against that existing handle. Detach at :1985–2006 checks channel ownership, requests sender shutdown and joins it. terminals.rs:414–461 contains no sink lease or external attachment-owned process. grid_stream.rs:937–963 selects shutdown against the stream; :1022–1055 creates the pump from host.input_sequence without spawning a process or adopting another host connection. Thus none of the removed external-client reap/respawn barriers has a surviving viewer operation to protect.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:2628–2630, Terminal host / Grid streams, says exactly: "an attach to a host terminal from a client that can show grids is answered with stream kind `grid` and gets a sender task of its own in the forwarder's place". The SPEC.md Terminal experience section separately requires that a new terminal's intake be independent of viewers.

Caveats: this does not establish every runtime reconnect or re-adoption path is defect-free. No independent retired sink defects were investigated. No tests or reproductions executed. This revision supplies the original line reference, the requested feedback headings and an exact contract quotation; the originally considered stuck-output/client-overlap consequence is unchanged.

# Removed tmux sink lifecycle tests

Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR

Considered whether removing sink retry/reap/handoff tests causes stuck output, leaked clients or overlap during viewer reconnect. Viewer reconnect no longer creates or replaces an external reader. This rejects that specific removal concern; it does not certify every host reconnection or recovery test.

## Details

Suggested bucket: high if materially stuck output were established. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this removal. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the attachment-owned-reader premise, not execution evidence. proposed_drop: source refutation, pending the parent's independent check; no parent acceptance claimed. possible_cover: none known; prohibited coverage sources not searched.

The assigned deletion is patch lines 141–991, parent terminals.rs:3969 through the sink test ending before :4820. There are no surviving supervisor-source references to SessionSink, run_session_sink, SinkRegistry or sink_retry_delay. HostTerminal shares an Arc at hosts/terminal.rs:1226–1280. Its runtime starts at adoption (:1926), and Runtime::run (:3031–3053) owns the connection, independently of viewer tasks. SessionEntry retains its terminal (service/core.rs:4144–4152), and tabs retain theirs in the session's host-tab cell (core/host_tabs.rs:130–145, :249–280). Last-viewer detach therefore is not last-terminal-owner drop.

handlers.rs:1688–1717 resolves the existing terminal and requires grid support; :1935–1974 creates HostAttach and GridSender without adopting a host or spawning a process. Detach :1985–2006 joins the sender after checking channel ownership. terminals.rs:414–461 holds no sink lease. grid_stream.rs:937–963 selects sender shutdown; :1022–1055 creates an input pump from host.input_sequence; :1169–1175 cancels that pump on drop; :1201–1243 stops its in-process work and discards queued input not handed to the runtime. None reaps or replaces an external reader. The caller reports g118/g120 corroboration of this same narrow ownership conclusion; the cited source is the independent basis here.

Necessary behavior versus obsolete mechanics: the deleted process-reap, stale-reaper poisoning and same-session external-client handoff oracles target operations that no longer exist on viewer attach/detach. Recovery still matters, but it now belongs to the host runtime/re-adoption layer rather than an attachment sink. Synthesis checked core/host_handover.rs:1373–1377 (capped delay), :1390–1417 (supervisor-owned retry loop), :1433–1540 (agent/tab scheduling with saturating counts, no attempt-limit exit, retained backoff across success). Existing test source core/tests/host_terminals.rs:2359–2415 checks successful adoption retains attempt history and every unstable episode waits the reconnect window; :2710–2761 checks tab identity/order/scope and retry count survive adoption and the agent restart window. Unlike the removed sink's healthy-run-reset rule, the host retry policy deliberately keeps history (SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host / Across supervisor restarts: "The attempt count is kept for that session and launch (or session and tab id) even after success"). A missing sink-reset test is therefore not proof of a missing current-policy oracle. These checks establish actual replacement oracles for those particular behaviors, not full retry coverage.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:2628–2630, Terminal host / Grid streams: "an attach to a host terminal from a client that can show grids is answered with stream kind `grid` and gets a sender task of its own in the forwarder's place". Scope caveat: no complete proof of all runtime reconnect, scheduling, cancellation or test paths is claimed; only the removed attachment sink roles and readily checkable related assumptions were resolved. Original suspected stuck-output/client-overlap consequence preserved. No runtime tests or reproductions executed; no independent retired-code defects investigated.
